dos: Keep your team together and follow organizer directions.
Share your team's ideas with one another and submit answers through the app.
Keep track of clues and unlock codes your team earns.
donts: Share clues, answers, or unlock codes with other teams.
Interfere with another team's work or try to bypass or alter the game.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.puzzle:
Symmetry I keep in all but one small thing:
A second sleeper broke my perfect plan.
Beside a bending river I do cling,
And lesser tombs have called me sister, when they can.

places.name: Red Fort
places.puzzle:
Red-coated twin am I, but not alone;
My elder cousin wears the same attire.
My greatest gate doth face a city not my own,
And one who moved his throne raised me up higher.

places.name: Qutub Minar
places.puzzle:
Some say I called the faithful, others, crowed of war;
Mine tiers each wear a different garb of stone.
None may ascend my stair, since a crowded day of sorrow,
Yet ancient words climb up my sides, alone.

places.name: India Gate
places.puzzle:
A gate through which no door doth ever swing,
I bear the names of those who fell abroad.
Though "gate" is part of both our names, I bring
No harbour to my feet. Mine is a road.

places.name: Golden Temple
places.puzzle:
Two lands lay claim to golden halls of prayer:
One by a spiral path, in southern ground;
Mine is the one whose water is the heart,
And at whose threshold every soul is fed.

places.name: Gateway of India
places.puzzle:
No road leads up to me, but water's edge;
A king I greeted who ne'er saw me done.
Through me a regiment last crossed the ledge,
When foreign rule was over and the day was won.

places.name: Hawa Mahal
places.puzzle:
No rooms behind me, only face and show;
A crown of some blue god, they say I wear.
My city's walls and I in matching colours glow,
Though not the lake-palace that floats in air.

places.name: Amer Fort
places.puzzle:
Above a lake I sit, with glass to light the night;
My sister keeps a higher watch than I.
Yet 'twas by elephant that visitors came to sight
My courts, and some still ride them, passing by.

places.name: Charminar
places.puzzle:
A number and a tower make my name;
Four there be, though some would count them more.
A vow against a plague did give me fame,
And a great mosque and a palace stand next door.

places.name: Ajanta Ellora Caves
places.puzzle:
Not one, but two, and each a different tale:
One painted, hidden till a hunter's chase;
One carved from top to bottom, without fail,
Three faiths in one rock's quiet, sacred space.

places.name: Mysore Palace
places.puzzle:
Not he of the garden-city, aping Windsor's keep,
Nor he whose lake-side halls now host the guest.
A flame once took my wooden elder; now I leap
In lamplight on a festival night's crest.

places.name: Victoria Memorial
places.puzzle:
A Queen I honour, yet her name's also on a station,
In a city on the western shore.
But I am whiter, and in marble's elation
I shelter statues, with a winged guard on top.

places.name: Sun Temple (Konark)
places.puzzle:
Three suns there are, in three different lands:
One in the west with a stepped and sacred pool,
One in a northern valley, in ruins, where it stands,
Mine hath wheels that tell the hour, as a rule.

places.name: Hampi Ruins
places.puzzle:
The name thou knowest is not the name I bore,
Nor is mine the capital's earlier tale.
A kingdom fell, and I lie in ruin's lore,
Yet pillars sing, and boulders watch the dale.

places.name: Mahabodhi Temple
places.puzzle:
Not where he was born, nor where he preached,
Nor where he left the world, but where he woke.
A cousin of the tree grows far, and is reached
By pilgrims overseas, who also make their yoke.

places.name: Sanchi
places.puzzle:
Lions guard mine gates, yet not the lions of thy coin;
They're cousins of the ones that crown the land.
No portrait of the Teacher doth my gates enjoin,
But symbols tell his tale, on every hand.

places.name: Kohima War Cemetery
places.puzzle:
A war in two places, and two silent fields:
I'm the hillside one, where a tennis court was fought,
My sister lies upon a valley's shield,
And both keep names of those who came and fought.

places.name: Mehrangarh Fort
places.puzzle:
Above a blue-washed city I preside,
But not the desert fort that's golden-hued.
A poet said that giants served as guide
To raise me, and my walls were thus imbued.

places.name: Bundi Stepwells
places.puzzle:
Not the famed well of a northern town,
Nor the one with a hundred steps in the west:
I am a queen's work, and I go down
Beside my many sisters, who are blessed.

places.name: Nalanda
places.puzzle:
Not the first of learned seats, nor the last;
Taxila's sister, Vikramshila's kin.
Monks from afar walked in my halls, and passed
Long years in study, ere the fire came in.
